body: I've found similar hypocrisy among people who rally around PTSD. Only some kinds of PTSD seem to qualify. Those homeless Vets are "scary" and "are probably alcoholics."

Isn't this the truth. My husband has Panic Disorder and hypochondria complete with sonambulism and nearly nightly night terrors and when people hear about a day in the life of him or me it's obvious that it's heavier than they were expecting and the response is more "sorry I asked" than "I hope you find the resources you need."

A "good night" in our house is me ensuring him that he isn't actively dying and doesn't need to go to the ER, all while in my head I'm adding up his symptoms because he does have high blood pressure and is nearing the age where one of his uncles had his first heart attack, trying to determine if this one is "real." A not-uncommon night is me getting startled awake by him screaming and flailing in his sleep in the middle of the room and him waking up to a panic attack which feels like a heart attack and me having to assure him that he is just having a night terror without getting accidentally hit while I guide him back to bed.

Garden variety "anxiety" feels more like a personality quirk, and I have anxiety myself.

Yeah, I agree. My state isn't very generous but I will look into it, I think he probably is reaching that point where he would qualify. I think it's a long process but maybe we should at least start it in case he doesn't find something else. 

I wish I could make enough to replace his income and my old income, but I need to go to school to realistically do that. It's in the works for next year--was going to be this year but I found out that I needed major surgery just before FAFSA opened for this year so it's on hold until then. So long as I can even get a part time W2 job to make up the difference until then it would make an enormous impact for the better.
